Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36559: test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex

2f7622e3f6f7ef431a7d5ec522958da62f33cec4 test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex (Kevin Ravensberg)

Pull request description:

  `feature_anchors.py` builds the expected `anchors.dat` substring from each peer's port with `hex(port)[2:]`, which is not zero-padded. The port is serialized as two bytes, so for ports below 4096 the expected string is one hex digit short and `assert ip_port in anchors_hex` fails.

  This only shows up with a non-default port range, for example when avoiding local listeners:

  ```
  TEST_RUNNER_PORT_MIN=1100 test/functional/feature_anchors.py
  ```

  fails on master with `AssertionError` at the `assert ip_port in anchors_hex` line and passes with this change; the default range still passes.

  ---
  Disclosure: AI (Claude Fable 5.1) was used to find this issue and to draft this PR.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36407: test: make orphanage_dos_many fill the orphanage

86ff13a0af0679ee0c725bac9c64c3e373cb0283 test: make orphanage_dos_many fill the orphanage (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  `test_orphanage_dos_many` checks that a normal peer's orphan survives while DoS peers flood the orphanage. I found that the orphanage never fills: the 60 peers send the same 51 orphans as `tx`, and a `tx` already held as an orphan is dropped in `ReceivedTx` without recording its sender. The orphanage peaks at 152 announcements against a limit of 3000, so nothing is evicted.

  Here the first peer sends the orphans and the other 59 announce them by `inv`, which does add them as announcers. The test now asserts that the orphanage holds 3000 announcements, instead of asserting on what it sends. It takes about as long as before.

  If `LimitOrphans` is changed to evict the normal peer's orphan first, the test used to pass and now fails. (`test_orphanage_dos_large` already catches that change.)

  Found while porting these tests to https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-node-tests.

  *Made with my usual tools: a computer, the Internet and an LLM. The mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36341: wallet: return error from bitcoin-wallet create

f64d33672fe1488b49254a634cbecfd9ce4ca179 wallet: return error from bitcoin-wallet create (Kanan)

Pull request description:

  `bitcoin-wallet create` exits with status 0 even when the wallet couldn't be created:

  ```
  $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -wallet=w1 create   # first time, ok
  $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -wallet=w1 create
  Failed to create database path '.../regtest/wallets/w1'. Database already exists.
  $ echo $?
  0
  ```

  In `ExecuteWalletToolFunc` the `create` branch only does something when `MakeWallet` succeeds and then falls through to `return true`. The other commands (`info`, `dump`, `createfromdump`) all return false on failure. So scripts that check the exit code think the wallet was created.

  This returns false when `MakeWallet` fails, the same way `info` does. The added check in `tool_wallet.py` runs `create` on the existing wallet `foo` and expects exit code 1. It fails on master (`not(0 == 1)`) and passes with the fix.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36339: wallet: avoid int overflow in listtransactions

9cff82fd5b15bc2aa2c7778b61212876433a8219 wallet: avoid int overflow in listtransactions (Kanan)

Pull request description:

  `listtransactions` adds `count` and `skip` as `int`. Each one is checked to be non-negative, but their sum can still go past INT_MAX:

  ```
  bitcoin-cli -regtest listtransactions "*" 2147483647 1
  ```

  On master this crashes the node. The overflowed sum is negative, so the loop stops after the first entry. The clamp after the loop overflows the same way and doesn't fix `nCount`, so `push_backV` gets an iterator range about 2^31 elements before `rend()`. UBSan reports `signed integer overflow: 1 + 2147483647` at transactions.cpp:584, and ASan then reports a BUS error in `UniValue::push_backV`.

  This parses `count` and `skip` as `uint32_t` through `self.Arg` (which also handles the defaults and rejects negative values, so the manual checks go away) and adds them up in 64 bits, where the sum can't overflow. The functional test calls `listtransactions` with count + skip above INT_MAX and up to UINT32_MAX and checks the results match a normal-sized request. It times out on master (the node crashes) and passes with the fix. I also ran it on an ASan/UBSan build.

  `listrawtransactions` counts differently and isn't affected.

  Since 9f66ac7cf1, only empty headers, headers that connect to the block index, or a valid low-work sync continuation count as a response to an outstanding getheaders.   It adds a test case that sends an unconnecting header again right after the previous getheaders and check that no new getheaders goes out. Then advance mocktime past `HEADERS_RESPONSE_TIME` and check that a getheaders is sent again.

  It kills the mutant https://mutanthub.space/mutants/3744.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36368: bitcoin-tx: reject in and outscript arguments with too many separators

2fef1db4f88a02efd666da41bc3641345940669d bitcoin-tx: reject in and outscript arguments with too many separators (Bruce0X)

Pull request description:

  `outscript=VALUE:SCRIPT[:FLAGS]` only reads the flags when there are exactly three fields (bitcoin-tx.cpp:482). With a trailing or extra `:` the flags are silently dropped:

  ```
  $ bitcoin-tx -create outscript=0:OP_DROP:S nversion=1
  010000000001000000000000000017a91471ed53322d470bb96657deb786b94f97dd46fb158700000000  # P2SH, as requested
  $ bitcoin-tx -create outscript=0:OP_DROP:S: nversion=1
  0100000000010000000000000000017500000000  # bare OP_DROP output, exit code 0
  ```

  So a typo gives a transaction paying to the raw script instead of the P2SH/P2WSH wrapper, with no error. `outpubkey` and `outaddr` already reject extra fields with "TX output missing or too many separators".

  This rejects `outscript` arguments with more than three fields, and `in=TXID:VOUT[:SEQUENCE_NUMBER]` arguments with more than three fields (which were accepted the same way), both with a general "Invalid format, expected ..." error. `bitcoin-util-test.json` gets a case for each; they fail on master (exit code 0) and pass with the fix, and `tool_utils.py` passes.

  AI tools were used to help find this issue and to prepare the patch and test.

test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex

The test builds the expected anchors.dat substring from the peer's port
with hex(port)[2:], which is not zero-padded. The port is serialized as
two bytes, so for ports below 4096 the expected string is one hex digit
short and the assertion fails:

    TEST_RUNNER_PORT_MIN=1100 test/functional/feature_anchors.py

Format the port as four hex digits instead.
